text: Suppose a first-quadrant spectral sequence has $E_2^{p,q}=0$ for all $q\neq 0$ (a single nonzero row). What follows?
choices: The spectral sequence fails to converge
$H^n\cong E_2^{0,n}$, read off the fiber edge
explanation: Each $d_r$ with $r\geq 2$ lowers the $q$-degree by $r-1\geq 1$, so with only the row $q=0$ nonzero every differential vanishes: the sequence collapses, $E_2=E_\infty$, and $H^n\cong E_2^{n,0}$. Reading $E_2^{0,n}$ is the single-column case; collapse is precisely why convergence does hold; and there are no Tor corrections because only one graded piece is nonzero.
